newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares edge up, seen firmer.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares edge up, seen firmer.

text.p: Leading Russian shares firmed in early trade on Wednesday after a weak start to the day, and traders saw the market closing firmer on sustained local and foreign demand.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index opened slightly off at 338.93 after closing on Tuesday at 339.04.
But traders saw the market picking up towards the end of the day although a correction was possible.
"I think a lot of people would like to see the market drift a bit lower as there are quite a few unsatisfied orders in blue chip stocks," said Martin Diggle, director at Brunswick.
"But I don't think it will move very much lower because there's quite a lot of demand, especially for blue chips. I would expect to see index close slightly higher."

National power company UES EESR.RTS rose to $0.2773 at GMT 0830 from $0.2750 on Tuesday and regional power utility Mosenergo MSNG.RTS edged up to $1.354 from $1.351. Automotive producer Kamaz KMAZ.RTS rose to $1.50 from $1.46.

"It's a boom market. There was a little correction in the morning, but the market is growing," said Alexander Fonarkov, a trader at Regent European Securities, adding that second tier stocks were also doing well.
